title: JANUS Cultural Mechanics — vocabulary-independent cross-text transfer test R2
research_question: Do the extracted state-transition machines recur in unrelated narratives when source-specific vocabulary is removed and matching is performed only on actor roles, state changes, causal order, recurrence and closure behavior?

anti_overfit_protocol.strict_pass_rule: At least 80% of ordered operators survive with no actor-role inversion and no dependence on source-specific nouns.
anti_overfit_protocol.partial_pass_rule: At least 50% of ordered operators survive, but one or more operators are absent, inverted or require abstraction.
anti_overfit_protocol.inversion_rule: The same state variables and recurrence exist, but the terminal operator reverses the parent machine's effect.
anti_overfit_protocol.fail_rule: Surface thematic similarity exists without preservation of ordered state transitions.

evidence_source.evidence_summary: Official synopsis presents asymmetric attachment and a retrospective traversal through different periods of the relationship to determine what failed.

candidate_corpus.title: Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind

evidence_source.evidence_summary: Official synopsis centers on a turbulent relationship, reciprocal memory erasure, reliving prior relationship states and rediscovery of attachment during erasure.
Public-domain text and summary support a long-lived projection onto a person from the past, with the imagined model accumulating significance beyond the present reality.
The protagonist repeatedly experiences the same day, recognizes the recursion, updates behavior and self-model, and ultimately changes rather than merely repeating the old state.

A constrained departure window, rare travel documents, relationship conflict and final resource transfer converge at the airport; the documents have practical and symbolic value but lack the full prior-loss recovery chain.
A lonely person develops an intimate bond with an adaptive artificial agent; the relationship deepens while the two participants' capabilities and models increasingly diverge.
Two partners pursue strong creative ideals while their relationship and ambitions interact; the work emphasizes tension between attachment, aspiration and realized life paths.
A protagonist inhabits a repeated constructed social environment, detects inconsistencies, revises his world-model and acts against the structure that previously constrained him.

tests.reason: The official synopsis directly establishes asymmetric attachment and retrospective reconstruction of the relationship. The machine survives after all source-specific nouns are removed.
Recurrence, vulnerability and relationship reconstruction are strong, but the central asymmetry is not the same: both participants were substantially involved.
A close bond develops while participant models and capabilities diverge, but the mismatch arises from evolving ontology/capacity rather than a simple commitment asymmetry.
A large model gap exists between projected relationship reality and actual present conditions, but the operator chain is dominated by one participant's projection.
The projected model of a past relationship becomes more powerful than the present target can satisfy. This is a near-clean transfer of ideal-template versus reality divergence.
Ideal templates are attached to future creative lives rather than only to a person; realized life paths diverge from the imagined combined future.
An initially bounded model of the partner becomes inadequate as the partner evolves beyond it; the idealized model and actual entity increasingly diverge.
One participant maintains a romanticized template that conflicts with the other's stated model, but the coupled/two-sided aspect is weak.
The relationship is actively removed from memory, then re-encountered through surviving structure; new knowledge does not automatically eliminate the possibility of re-entry.
Repeated exposure produces explicit self-model revision, but instead of stabilizing the old pattern, the revision changes behavior enough to exit the recursion.
Repeated routines reveal anomalies; the protagonist updates his world/self model and acts to escape the constructed recurrence rather than normalize it.

machine_tests.discovery: The original stabilizer is one branch of a more general recursion engine. Self-model update can either preserve the attractor or generate an escape trajectory.

tests.reason: The narrative explicitly moves back and forth through different periods of the relationship, making repeated reconstruction the organizing structure rather than incidental exposition.
The fading-memory traversal repeatedly exposes relationship states; structural revisitation raises the importance of the same relational core.
The same day is structurally replayed many times. Repetition becomes the dominant memory and causal scaffold.
Repeated routines accumulate enough anomaly weight to reveal the hidden system; repetition functions as detection rather than merely reinforcement.
A narrow departure window and rare travel documents culminate in a decisive transfer. Scarcity and prior events amplify value, but there is no clean reversal of an expected permanent-loss state.
Symbolic objects exist, but no ordered departure-resource-recovery-transfer chain matches the parent machine.
Memory recovery is narratively central, but it is not a transferable resource delivered during a departure gate.

machine_tests.discovery: The full prior-loss reversal appears source-specific in this corpus. A shorter submachine survives: constrained departure -> rare resource -> transfer -> symbolic/practical amplification.

cross_machine_discoveries.finding: The most transferable variable is not romance but divergence between two internal models of the same relation, target or future.
Recursion plus self-observation is a supermachine with at least two outcomes: ATTRACTOR_STABILIZATION and ESCAPE_BY_MODEL_UPDATE.
Repeated narrative structure can increase semantic weight even when the medium has no refrain or repeated wording.
The projection target can be a partner, a remembered past, a future career/life configuration, or another adaptive entity.
The rare-resource transfer kernel transfers, but the complete loss-reversal plus symbolic-gift sequence has not yet survived a strict unrelated-corpus test.

negative_controls.rule: Shared themes such as attachment, aspiration or loss do not count if operator order is absent.
Shared nouns or metaphors do not increase transfer score.
If causal agency changes actor without an explicit generalized mapping, strict transfer fails.
A machine with the same recurrence but opposite terminal effect is labeled INVERSION, not silently counted as an exact match.

verdict.key_result: The source text contains several machines that survive vocabulary removal and medium changes. The strongest discovery is the recursion/self-model supermachine with two terminal branches: stabilization or escape.

next_gate: R3_BLIND_MECHANICS_CLASSIFIER: freeze PM01-PM05 names and chains, hide work titles, feed plot-event graphs from at least 20 unrelated works, score operator-order matches first, then reveal titles. Require negative controls and predeclared thresholds before promoting any machine.
